subject: reasoning
question: A, B, C, D, G, H and I are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. Only one person sits between D and G when counted from the left of G. H sits third to the right of I. C sits third to the left of A. H sits to the immediate right of C. B is not an immediate neighbour of C. How many people sit between B and G when counted from the right of B?
solution:
**Given: ** A, B, C, D, G, H and I are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table.

Only one person sits between D and G when counted from the left of G.

H sits third to the right of I. C sits third to the left of A.

H sits to the immediate right of C. B is not an immediate neighbour of C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8978d7f70922976ca022ddaf3258e2768379088a5c05307109f660daaf81a3f4.png] 

Thus, Only three people sit between B and G when counted from the right of B.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
